definition: A frontier model appearing across 5 sources as the reference ceiling that trained open models are measured against, and occasionally as an annotator. Its measured positions here: it is the strongest system on the archive's coding-agent tables, with a trained 7B model narrowing the gap to it from 56.4 to 43.3 points without closing it, and at 42.9 percent on a competition tier where every trained system scores 0.0; it holds the best macro accuracy on an industrial-safety benchmark (89.5) where a fine-tuned 9B model takes the best micro; and it appears as a data augmenter and as a group-type classifier inside one training pipeline, which makes that pipeline's dynamics analysis contingent on its labelling.

evidence.note: Gives each retrieval step of a search agent a dense reward built from two ground-truth-conditioned signals — how much the step raised the model's likelihood of the correct answer, and how necessary the step looks in hindsight — and fuses them asymmetrically so that a step which helps locally but is redundant globally is discounted.
evidence.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent

evidence.note: Recasts long-document visual question answering as building an explicit evidence graph whose nodes are grounded document blocks and whose edges are reasoning dependencies, and verifies the graph causally — masking the evidence it cites flips 82.8% of correct answers while masking uncited evidence changes 9.6%.
evidence.title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning

evidence.note: Assigns credit in coding-agent RL by splitting each code diff into sub-diffs, matching semantically similar sub-diffs across rollouts to form advantage groups, and projecting the resulting diff-level advantage back onto the tokens that produced it.
evidence.title: DiDPO: Diff-in-Diff Policy Optimization for Coding Agent Training

evidence.note: Builds an industrial-safety reasoning benchmark from two pipelines -- program execution over safety scene graphs, and evidence graphs extracted from real accident-investigation reports -- and shows that general multimodal capability does not transfer to it while a 9B model fine-tuned on its chain-of-thought split matches frontier systems.
evidence.title: SafeSceneReason: A Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Connecting Industrial Hazards with Accident Knowledge

evidence.note: Fine-tunes a 1.7B model to read structured summaries of a time series and allocate ensemble weights across candidate forecasters, trained by SFT on rule-generated chains of thought and then by GRPO with a bounded reciprocal reward that keeps a continuous error gap from collapsing the group advantage.
evidence.title: REATS: LLM Reasoning-based Ensemble Learning for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting

name: GPT-5.5
